name: core.openwop.workflows.content
description: Real-work workflow pack (RFC 0013, ADR 0190 Phase 3) — the Content & Monitoring cluster: watch an RSS/Atom feed for new items and watch any web page for changes, each pairing a schedule trigger with durable seen-state in host KV storage (deterministic per-source key; the first run treats everything as new and seeds the state). NO host RSS poller exists — adding an 'rss' ingestion source to /v1/trigger-subscriptions is RFC 0099 wire territory (see ADR 0190) — so these chains ARE the poller: pair each with a Schedule and the scheduler does the polling. Authored over shipped node typeIds (core.trigger.schedule + core.openwop.http.fetch + core.storage.kv-get/kv-set + core.ai.chatCompletion + core.openwop.integration.notification-push). No external sends — digests are in-app notifications, so no approval gate is needed. All tenant values are run parameters (replay-deterministic).
author: openwop

chains.label: Feed Watcher & Digest
chains.description: Watch an RSS/Atom feed and get a digest of only the NEW items since the last run: fetch the feed, compare against the items already seen (kept in durable storage), summarize what's new, and remember it for next time. Pair with a Schedule to poll on a cadence; the first run seeds the seen-list, so expect everything to be new once.

feedUrl.description: The RSS/Atom feed URL to watch.

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's LLM nodes. Frozen into this chain's AI nodes when the workflow is created (ADR 0498 — a concrete provider is what keeps replay deterministic). Override at instantiation to use a different vendor or your own BYOK provider; whichever you pick, the workspace needs a key for it — the workflow will not fall back to another provider on its own.

model.description: Model id for this chain's LLM nodes. Must be advertised by `provider` in the host catalog; override at instantiation.

scheduleCron.description: Cron expression for when this workflow runs (e.g. `0 9 * * 1` = Mondays 09:00).

config.systemPrompt: You are a feed-watch differ. Input 1 is raw RSS/Atom XML from {{params.feedUrl}}; input 2 is last run's stored output (may be empty — then every item is new; if it contains sections, the authoritative seen-list is the one under 'SEEN'). Output two sections: NEW ITEMS — title, link, and a one-line summary for each item not in the seen list (or 'No new items.'); SEEN — the updated full list of item ids/links (previous plus new), one per line.

digest.description: The new-items digest (and the refreshed seen-list in storage).

chains.label: Page Change Watch
chains.description: Watch any web page (competitor pricing, docs, a changelog) and get told WHAT changed, not just that it changed: fetch the page, compare against the last snapshot in durable storage, summarize the differences that matter, and save the new snapshot. Pair with a Schedule; the first run just takes the baseline snapshot.

focus.description: What kinds of changes matter to you.

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's LLM nodes. Frozen into this chain's AI nodes when the workflow is created (ADR 0498 — a concrete provider is what keeps replay deterministic). Override at instantiation to use a different vendor or your own BYOK provider; whichever you pick, the workspace needs a key for it — the workflow will not fall back to another provider on its own.

model.description: Model id for this chain's LLM nodes. Must be advertised by `provider` in the host catalog; override at instantiation.

scheduleCron.description: Cron expression for when this workflow runs (e.g. `0 9 * * 1` = Mondays 09:00).

config.systemPrompt: You are a page-change analyst watching {{params.pageUrl}} for changes to: {{params.focus}}. Input 1 is the freshly fetched page; input 2 is last run's stored output (may be empty — then this run is the baseline; if it contains sections, compare against the one under 'SNAPSHOT'). Output: CHANGES — the meaningful differences, each with a one-line why-it-matters (or 'No meaningful changes.' / 'Baseline captured.'); SNAPSHOT — the current page content distilled to the substance worth comparing next time.

report.description: The change report (and the refreshed snapshot in storage).
